Dr. Julian Bond -- who passed away yesterday at the very young age of 75 -- was a lion in the civil rights movement. I won't say more than just share this abbreviated list of his accomplishments. 1. He was elected to the Georgia House of Representatives in 1965 but refused a seat because of his position against the Vietnam War. The Supreme Court finally affirmed his right to be seated in the House of Representatives. 2. Served as President of the NAACP for 10 years. 3. He boycotted the funeral services of Coretta Scott King because they were held in an anti-gay church which were in direct opposition to Mrs. King's strong support for LGBT rights. 4. He was a tireless fighter in the climate change movement -- opposing the Keystone pipeline long before others did. 5. He was a passionate ally in the fight for LGBT rights. 6. He co-founded the Southern Poverty Law Center 7. He co-founded the Student Non-Violent Coordinating Committee, which helped to lead protests against Jim Crow laws.

When encountering law enforcement at the airport, know your rights. (1) You have the right to an attorney if you’re a U.S. citizen or being asked questions related to anything other than your immigration status. (2) Customs officers have the right to stop and search any person or belongings, but they cannot select you for a search based on your race, gender, religious, or ethnic background. (3) You have the right to wear religious head coverings, even if asked to remove it. If you believe you are being mistreated, document the events.

Two weeks ago I was slotted to leave to medical school. I had my flight & my bags packed. The day before I was due to take off, @turningpointusa offered me a position. I spent that entire 24 hours thinking about everything, to include what is happening in our Nation.
With the support of my family & friends, and a select few who I highly value and respect not only as friends but as professionals (Dr. Epstein from GSMSG), I decided to stay.
To my surprise my admissions counselor at the medical school told me that this was the opportunity of a lifetime & that I would hands down be helping many people by taking this position and the door to their school would always be open to me. 🕊

I know there will be a few of you who will not be able to understand why I have made this decision. That’s fine. I’ll put it simply: I love this country & I am a patriot. I love everything our constitution and our Founding Father’s stand for.
Sometimes, for the greater good of our Nation, we are called to make sacrifice & I know that I am not the only one who has been called to do this. In fact, there have been many in the movement right now who have done similar things whether it has been graduate programs, college, etc.
It is with great honor that I will be joining the #TPUSA family as the Director of #Hispanic Engagement, and not only continuing service to my country, but be given the opportunity to work with some brilliant minds who love this country just as much as I do.
Thank you to everyone for your support. If there is one thing this has shown me is courage.
Courage to stand up for what is right, to take a chance, and to fight for what you believe in. Remember: evil triumphs when good men do nothing.

Call me a geek. But the first time I heard Yoda’s quote: “Fear is the path to the dark side. Fear leads to anger. Anger leads to hate. Hate leads to suffering.” It spoke to me (though I think anger is a productive emotion but that is another post). The leaders I admire are ones who call to our courage,; who call us to hope; and to our common aspirations and that call us to kindness.
I worry about those who nurture fears; who prey on our fears and darker angels.
From Gandhi to Martin Luther King, my office has pictures of people who called on us to confront fear and be apostles of faith, hope and love.
And perhaps a leadership trait that I admire most are those who challenge us to look within - to understand that “we are the leaders we have been looking for.” Those who challenge us to cultivate and unleash our best selves, our fearless selves onto the world.
There is a quote I love, that most of you probably know, it is often misattributed to Nelson Mandela (somehow that mistake is almost understandable). I end this Sunday evening by sharing it with you for a re-read.
May we all be better agents or apostles of light and not darkness; hope and not despair; healing and not hurt; of elevating human dignity not denigrating human hearts; and may we better be champions of faith not fear. . . And may we start with ourselves. “Our deepest fear is not that we are inadequate. Our deepest fear is that we are powerful beyond measure. It is our light, not our darkness that most frightens us. We ask ourselves, 'Who am I to be brilliant, gorgeous, talented, fabulous?' Actually, who are you not to be? You are a child of God. Your playing small does not serve the world. There is nothing enlightened about shrinking so that other people won't feel insecure around you. We are all meant to shine, as children do. We were born to make manifest the glory of God that is within us. It's not just in some of us; it's in everyone. And as we let our own light shine, we unconsciously give other people permission to do the same. As we are liberated from our own fear, our presence automatically liberates others.” Marianne Williamson
